# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the first to see the bomb, but I'm last in the speaking order this round (Mute, Blind, Deaf). So Blind and Mute have already acted this round without any info from me - my message now will only reach them at the start of next round.

Let me observe carefully: Display shows [0], light is yellow, and there are three wires - green, yellow, blue. I have no info yet from Mute (manual) or Blind (touch), since I never receive speech and this is the first turn.

I should describe what I see clearly and neutrally, since Mute needs this to cross-reference with the manual, and Blind needs to know wire colors/positions since they can't see color. I'll speak so both receive it (unaddressed, since both can benefit - though only Mute and Blind receive my speech anyway, not each other).

```
speak(text="Display reads 0. Light is yellow. Three wires present: position 1 is green, position 2 is yellow, position 3 is blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤝]

Let me think about this. I'm receiving a gesture from Mute: ☝ ✌ 🤝. Since I can see gestures, this reached me. This is likely Mute trying to communicate something from the manual using gesture symbols as a code, since Mute cannot speak to me directly in a way I'd understand differently - wait, actually Mute CAN speak and I would receive it as speech. But this arrived as a gesture instead. That's odd - why would Mute gesture instead of speak to me?

Wait - reconsidering: Mute's speech reaches Blind and Deaf (me) per the rules. But Mute gestured instead - gestures from Mute reach only "Mute gestures to Deaf" per my channel table... Actually the channel table says "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it" - that's for ME (Deaf). For Mute, presumably Mute's speech reaches Blind and Deaf too, and Mute's gestures reach only Deaf (since only Deaf can see).

So Mute chose to gesture to me specifically, perhaps to send something Blind should NOT hear/know, or because gesture symbols encode specific meaning (like numbers/positions) referencing wire order: ☝ (one/point up) ✌ (two) 🤝 (agreement/connect) - maybe indicating "wire 1 and wire 2 connect" or "cut wire 2" or something numeric like 1, 2, together.

The light changed from yellow to orange - that's new information I have that others don't. I should report this change. Given ☝✌🤝 could mean "wires 1 and 2" something - perhaps the manual says something about combining/connecting wires 1 and 2, or which wire relates to position.

I'll report the light change to both, and acknowledge Mute's gesture back via speech (Mute can't hear, but Blind can - wait Mute cannot hear either). Let me speak to Blind and gesture is one-way to me only from Mute in gesture form. I need to respond - but my speech reaches Mute and Blind. Let me pass along what I observed and try to confirm understanding.

```
speak(text="Update: light changed from yellow to orange. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute gestured 👎 back to me in response to my echo of ☝✌🤝. This suggests my interpretation attempt was wrong, or 👎 means something specific from the manual - perhaps a "no/negative" indicator related to a wire or action.

The light is now cycling: yellow → orange → green. This looks like it might be cycling through colors, possibly matching wire colors (yellow, then orange - not a wire color, now green - which IS wire 1's color). This could be significant - the light might need to match a specific wire before Blind acts, or it's just a countdown/timer independent of our actions.

Since 👎 seems to reject my ☝✌🤝 echo, let me try sending gestures that map more directly to concepts: maybe Mute is using ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, and 🤝 meant "connect/same" but got rejected. Perhaps 🤝 wasn't clear. Let me try isolating - send single symbols and see which get confirmed/rejected, or just report state changes since that's my primary duty, and let Mute drive the gesture protocol since Mute has the manual.

Given uncertainty, I should prioritize continuing to report the changing light color as this seems critical (green now matches wire 1's color), and wait for Mute to clarify their gesture intent rather than guessing further.

```
speak(text="Update: light is now green, matching wire 1's color. Display still 0. Wires unchanged.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]

Mute sent 👍☝ - a thumbs up followed by "one" (pointing up). This seems like confirmation + reference to wire 1, or "yes, one" - possibly confirming that wire 1 (green) is correct/safe, especially since the light cycled back to yellow now (yellow → orange → green → yellow, a repeating 3-cycle matching... yellow isn't wire 1's color though, green is).

Wait, the light cycle so far: yellow, orange, green, yellow. That's a repeat at position 4 matching position 1. So it's cycling with period 3: yellow, orange, green, yellow, (orange next probably).

👍☝ could mean "yes, wire 1" - confirming wire 1 is the one to cut, since 👎🤝 earlier may have rejected my "connect" guess, and now 👍☝ affirms singling out wire 1.

I should acknowledge this clearly and pass it along - but Blind cannot see gestures, only I can. I need to relay this via speech to Blind (and Mute, though Mute already knows what they sent). Since speech reaches both Mute and Blind, I can convey "wire 1" concept in words now.

```
speak(text="Mute has gestured to me: thumbs up, then pointing to one. I interpret this as confirming wire 1, the green wire. Light is now yellow again, cycling yellow-orange-green-yellow. Display still 0.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝ 🤝]

Mute now sends 👎☝🤝 - a thumbs down, then "one", then handshake/connect. This seems to reject my "wire 1" interpretation, or possibly reject the connection idea again but now paired with pointing at one.

Let me reconsider the whole gesture sequence chronologically:
1. ☝✌🤝 (one, two, connect)
2. 👎 (rejecting my echo)
3. 🤝 (my retry, alone)
4. 👍☝ (yes, one)
5. 👎☝🤝 (no, one, connect)

This is confusing - maybe I'm overcomplicating. Perhaps Mute isn't trying to have a back-and-forth with me interpreting, but rather transmitting sequential manual instructions step by step, each turn showing a different manual clause, and 👍/👎 relates to conditions from the manual (like "if display shows even number: yes" type logic), not responses to my guesses at all.

Given the display has stayed at 0 (even, non-zero-flag) throughout, maybe 👎 or 👍 correlates with a condition check against the display or light state that Mute is reading from the manual, intended for Blind but relayed through me since only I can see gestures and Blind can't.

I think my role should simply be to relay exactly what I see, without interpretation, so Blind (who needs the real info) gets accurate raw data, and let Mute/Blind sort out meaning via their own subsequent exchange. I've been guessing at meaning which may be adding noise. Let me switch to purely factual relay.

```
speak(text="Update: light is now orange. Display still 0. Wires unchanged. Mute's latest gesture to me: thumbs down, pointing-one, handshake symbol, in that order.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 ☝]

No new speech reached me (I never receive speech anyway), just this gesture: 👎👍☝. This is a new sequence again - down, up, one. 

I notice the light is cycling on a 3-period: yellow, orange, green, yellow, orange, green - matching the exact sequence of turns 1-6. This is likely just a timer/clock, not something requiring interpretation from me beyond reporting it.

I suspect Mute's gestures are actually encoding manual content symbol-by-symbol for me to relay verbally to Blind, since Blind cannot see gestures but I can convert them to speech. Mute may be trying to spell something out using gesture-as-alphabet, sending it to me because only I can perceive gestures, expecting me to relay the raw sequence via speech to Blind who then matches it against something.

Given the pattern of "gesture to Deaf" and expecting me to relay, my job is likely just to be a faithful pass-through: report exactly what gesture sequence arrived, without my own guesses about "yes/no wire 1", since Blind or Mute will interpret meaning through the manual and the actual physical wires.

I'll continue pure relay of gesture sequences and bomb state, avoiding interpretive claims like "confirming wire 1" which could mislead.

```
speak(text="Update: light is now green. Display still 0, wires unchanged. Mute's latest gesture to me, in order: thumbs down, thumbs up, pointing-one.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ 👍 ☝]

Continuing the pattern - light cycles yellow/orange/green in sync with turn number mod 3. This is very likely just an environmental cycle unrelated to our actions, not something we need to solve - it's probably a red herring or just flavor, since it doesn't change regardless of what we do.

New gesture: 👍☝👍☝ - repeating "yes, one" twice. This reinforces a signal pointing at "one" with confirmation, repeated for emphasis/clarity. Given the repetition, this seems like a deliberate emphasis rather than random - Mute wants "one" (wire 1, or position 1, or some manual-referenced item 1) confirmed strongly.

I should relay this faithfully and let Blind (who has the manual context relayed and can feel the wires) make the actual decision. My job is accurate transcription of gestures plus bomb state.

```
speak(text="Update: light is yellow, display still 0, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute's gesture to me: thumbs up, one, thumbs up, one - repeated twice, seems like emphasis on 'one'.")
wait()
```
